findings.title: Write lock does not recheck cache and is held across asset I/O
findings.body: GetWebAssets snapshots entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, drops the lock, then later takes the write lock and always reloads and assigns the global. It never re-reads the cache after Lock, so every caller that observed a nil cache (all of them at startup, and every call when cfg.Env == Dev) reloads assets-manifest.json while holding the exclusive lock. A later waiter whose load fails stores that nil result into entryPointAssetsCache and wipes a value another goroutine already published, so a successful load can be discarded and the next requests miss again. Because the exclusive lock spans the file read (and the CDN HTTP path if enabled), those redundant loads are fully serialized and also block cache hits that arrive while a load is in progress. After acquiring the write lock, return the existing cache when Env is not Dev and it is already set; only publish a non-nil successful result; and do not hold the mutex across the file or HTTP read.
